subject: AWS Marketplace sandbox metering + SaaS fulfillment: integration plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Amy Jenkins <amy.jenkins@amazon.com>, ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: AWS Marketplace sandbox metering + SaaS fulfillment: integration plan

Hi Amy / ACME team,

Following up from last week's sync — we want to kick off a focused sandbox QA run for AWS Marketplace metering + SaaS fulfillment (Acme Analytics deal). High-level asks:

- Confirm the entitlement test flow in AWS sandbox (how buyer entitlements are surfaced to the SaaS seller).
- Confirm the fulfillment webhook contract and which fields will be present for usage records and entitlement events.
- Agree on a short test matrix and a 48-hour test window.

Proposed timeline:
- Dec 8–9: internal engineering run + AWS sandbox validation
- Dec 10: joint run with ACME to simulate purchases and entitlement propagation

Attached: metering-test-plan-v1.xlsx (draft test cases), and an initial mapping doc we'll populate (aws-entitlement-mapping.txt will follow).

Open questions for AWS:
- Do we need a separate seller-side product_code for sandbox vs production?
- Can AWS confirm whether entitlement events include customer-contact email or only buyer account id? ACME legal needs this for their PII review.

CCing Priyom and Marissa to coordinate the Redwood engineering and CS side.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of GTM Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
+1 650 555 0143

Attachments: metering-test-plan-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Amy Jenkins <amy.jenkins@amazon.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: marketplace-integration@amazon.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace sandbox metering + SaaS fulfillment: integration plan

Thanks Vanessa — happy to help get this moving. A few quick clarifications from the AWS partner side:

- Sandbox vs Prod: yes, you should use a separate product code for sandbox (prod codes are tied to entitlement records). We can provision a test product_code for ACME — I'll create an internal ticket and loop the marketplace integration team.
- Entitlement fields: sandbox fulfillment events will include the buyer account id and a buyer id; emails are not provided by default in the metering events for privacy reasons. If you need buyer email, you'll have to pass that through your own fulfillment flow or request explicit consent mapping.
- Fulfillment API: we recommend using the SaaS Subscriptions APIs for entitlement validation + the Metering Service for usage records. Metering records use product_code, dimension, quantity, and a timestamp.

I've opened ticket TKT-987654 for provisioning and a sandbox product_code. Marketplace integration (marketplace-integration@amazon.com) can confirm the exact test SKU and provide the sandbox product_code once provisioned.

For the test matrix: AWS sandbox supports immediate provisioning of test entitlements; we'll need Redwood to emit a usage record after you receive the entitlement. We can do a short smoke test within a 24-hour window.

I'll try to schedule a quick call with marketplace-integration to hand off the provisioning.

—Amy
Amy Jenkins
Partner Development Manager, AWS Marketplace
amy.jenkins@amazon.com

Thanks Vanessa / Amy — quick internal note on implementation so everyone is aligned:

What Redwood will do (engineering checklist):
- Stand up a sandbox fulfillment endpoint to accept AWS entitlement callbacks (HTTP POST) and validate product_code + dimension.
- Implement entitlement-to-license mapping: we will map AWS buyer account id -> Redwood tenant_id in a small lookup table. Draft mapping file attached: aws-entitlement-mapping.txt.
- Emit a usage record to AWS Metering immediately after entitlement consumption (we will run both single-event and burst tests).
- Add an idempotency key on our side to protect against duplicate AWS fulfillment callbacks.

Marcus, can you own the billing adapter changes (invoice line mapping for AWS metered usage)? We'll need one sample invoice line for ACME (usage-based SKU) so procurement can sign off.

Proposed internal schedule: engineering smoke tests Dec 8–9; dress rehearsal Dec 10 (joint). I'll prepare the test harness and share credentials in the next note.

Attachments: aws-entitlement-mapping.txt (plain text)

—Priyom
Priyom Das

priyom_das@redwood.com

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace sandbox metering + SaaS fulfillment: integration plan

Hi Vanessa / Amy,

Thanks for the outline. A couple items ACME procurement/legal needs clarified before we can participate in the joint run:

- Billing model: ACME is evaluating the difference between a monthly-seat SaaS SKU vs. a pure metered usage SKU. Can Redwood provide one sample invoice line for each model (example dollar amounts are fine) and confirm what the buyer will see on the AWS invoice?
- PII and entitlements: Does the fulfillment event include any buyer PII? Per our privacy team, we cannot have buyer emails flow to third-party systems without explicit consent. If AWS only exposes buyer account id, we need a recommended mapping strategy so ACME can correlate buyer accounts to internal users without exposing PII.
- SOC 2 evidence: please attach your latest SOC 2 report (or a pointer). This is required for procurement sign-off.

If those are provided, we can join the dress rehearsal on Dec 10. Otherwise we need to postpone until Dec 15.

Best,
Erin Mullins
Procurement Lead, Acme Analytics
procurement@acme.io

(Amy — CCing you for the sandbox product_code question)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace sandbox metering + SaaS fulfillment: integration plan

Erin / Amy — thanks for the quick responses. Short summary and action items so everyone has a single source of truth: 

Summary:
- AWS will provision a sandbox product_code (Amy / marketplace-integration will confirm TKT-987654). Entitlement events in sandbox will include buyer account id (no email).
- Redwood will map buyer account id -> tenant_id using an internal mapping table; we will not store buyer email unless ACME provides explicit consent.
- Billing adapter: Redwood will emit usage records and provide a sample invoice line for both monthly-seat and metered-usage options. Marcus to share sample lines by EOD Dec 3.
- SOC 2: Marissa, can you attach the latest SOC 2 summary and a link to the full report under NDA? ACME needs this for procurement.

Action items:
- Amy/AWS: provision sandbox product_code and share test SKU (TKT-987654).
- Marcus: sample invoice lines (monthly-seat and metered) — due EOD 2026-12-03.
- Marissa: SOC 2 summary / NDA pointer — due EOD 2026-12-03.
- Priyom: share sandbox test harness creds and aws-entitlement-mapping.txt update — due by Dec 6.
- ACME (Erin): confirm whether you can accept buyer account id mapping (no email) or require an alternate approach — reply by Dec 4.

I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Dec 3 at 9:00 AM PT to review the provisioning steps and confirm the test window; invite incoming. If anyone cannot make that time, flag now.

Thanks all — excited to get this across the finish line.

Vanessa Ortiz
